title: Sudoku strategies
examples: Can you show me how to use the columns to help me?
What is the first thing I should look at when I start?
Is there a trick for when I get stuck on a box?

explain.say: Today we are learning about Sudoku puzzle strategies. You need to use logic to fill in the numbers. Remember that every number from one to nine must appear once.

items: Each row must have numbers one through nine.
Each column must have numbers one through nine.
Each 3x3 box must have numbers one through nine.

draw.text: Sudoku: 1-9 once per row, column, box

explain.say: First, we look at the rows. A row is any straight line across the puzzle. For example, if you look at the top row, you can only put the missing numbers there.
Next, we check the columns. A column is any straight line going up and down. If you look at the middle column, you must use a number not already there.
Then we look at the boxes. The puzzle is divided into nine small boxes. Each box must also have all numbers from one to nine.
Now we find single candidates. This means looking at one empty square. You check its row, column, and box to see which number can fit there.

draw.text: Single Candidate: Check all three areas

explain.say: In real life, this is like scheduling a party. You have nine guests, and you must make sure each guest gets a unique seat. You check the room layout to see where each person can sit.

faq.q: Do I have to check all three areas every time?
faq.a: Yes, you must check the row, the column, and the box for every empty square. This makes sure the number follows all the rules.
asks: Do I check rows, columns, and boxes together?

faq.q: What if two numbers can fit in a square?
faq.a: If two numbers can fit, you cannot place a number yet. You need to look at a different empty square nearby.
asks: When should I move to another square?

faq.q: Does the puzzle have a starting point?
faq.a: Sometimes the puzzle gives you a hint, but you should always use the rules to find the next number. Start anywhere and follow the logic.
asks: Is there an easy place to begin?

faq.q: What is the difference between a row and a column?
faq.a: A row goes across like reading a book. A column goes up and down like standing up straight. They are two different directions.
asks: How is a column different from a row?

faq.q: Can I use a pencil to write guesses?
faq.a: Yes, it is best to use a pencil to write your possible numbers. This way you can erase them if you are wrong.

facts: Sudoku puzzles use numbers from one to nine.
The grid is always divided into nine smaller boxes.
A number cannot repeat in any single row, column, or box.
Finding single candidates means checking all three constraints at once.

quiz.say: If a square's row already has a four and a seven, and its column has a four and a nine, what number is definitely missing from the box?
quiz.show: Row has 4, 7. Column has 4, 9. Box needs one number.

options.show: The number cannot be four, seven, or nine.
options.say: The number cannot be four, seven, or nine.

quiz.why: You checked the row and column to eliminate those numbers, leaving only one choice for the box.

wrong.0: This is tempting because two is a small, easy number to remember.
wrong.1: This is tempting because the numbers are in order.
wrong.3: This is tempting because one is often the first number you check.

quiz.say: A square is in the top row, the middle column, and the top-left box. Which rule limits the number there?
quiz.show: Top Row, Middle Column, Top-Left Box

options.show: Only the row limits the number.
options.say: Only the row limits the number.

options.show: Only the box limits the number.
options.say: Only the box limits the number.

options.show: All three rules limit the number.
options.say: All three rules limit the number.

quiz.why: You must check the row, the column, and the box because the number must follow all three rules.

wrong.0: You forgot to check the column and the box, which are also rules.
wrong.1: You ignored the row and column, which are also important rules.
wrong.2: Every number must follow all three rules to be correct.

quiz.say: If you find a square where only the number five can fit based on its row, column, and box, what should you do?

options.show: Circle the square and move on.
options.say: Circle the square and move on.

options.show: Write five, but use a lighter pencil.
options.say: Write five, but use a lighter pencil.

options.show: Write the number five in that square.
options.say: Write the number five in that square.

quiz.why: When only one number works for all three rules, that is your answer and you should write it down.

wrong.0: You are leaving an answer that you know for sure.
wrong.1: You should write it clearly because it is a confirmed answer.
wrong.2: You are ignoring a definite answer you just found.
